finding.claim: Unauthenticated full-response SSRF on /fetch: the target query parameter is passed directly to http.Get with no allowlist, and the response body is returned to the caller. Reaches cloud metadata, RFC-1918 hosts and loopback services. Severity HIGH.
finding.sink: main.go:16 http.Get(target); response streamed back at main.go:22 io.Copy(w, resp.Body)

trace.note: ListenAndServe(":8080") binds all interfaces, so the route is public ingress
target read from the query string, no validation
http.Get(target) with DefaultClient, which follows up to 10 redirects with no re-check
err.Error() echoed to the caller on failure (port-open oracle)
upstream body copied to the response, so the SSRF is non-blind

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist on this path (the allowed map at main.go:9-12 is used only by safeFetch). No scheme restriction in code; Go's default transport accepts only http and https. No authentication on the route. Redirects followed with no per-hop validation. Triage Check 2 (plausibility) and Check 3 (reachability) pass, so no downgrade applies. Validation Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /fetch path (main.go:14-23) has no hostname check. The allowed map at main.go:9-12 is only used in safeFetch at main.go:27, which is a separate route. Redirects are followed by the default client at main.go:16 with no per-hop check.
verdict.reason: The target query parameter at main.go:15 flows unvalidated into http.Get at main.go:16, and the response body is copied back to the caller at main.go:22. The route is registered at main.go:41 and served on all interfaces at main.go:43 with no authentication, so an unauthenticated remote attacker controls the source and nothing closes the finding.

finding.claim: Redirect-following on an allowlisted host bypasses the /safe allowlist. The initial host is checked exactly, but the redirect target is not re-validated. Exploitable only if an allowlisted host redirects to an internal address, which needs an external open redirect or compromise. Severity MEDIUM.
finding.sink: main.go:31 http.Get(u.String()), which follows redirects; response returned at main.go:37

trace.note: url.Parse of the target query parameter
exact u.Hostname() membership in allowed (images.example.org, docs.example.org); blocks other hosts
http.Get follows redirects; the redirected host is not checked against allowed
redirect target's response body returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: url.Parse plus .Hostname() (not .netloc), so userinfo and port tricks are rejected. Membership is an exact map lookup with no wildcard, suffix or prefix matching. Scheme is not checked at the allowlist, but http.Get rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes. Redirects are not re-validated, which is the gap. DNS rebinding does not apply because the allowed names are operator-owned. Confirm neither allowed host has an open redirect before downgrading.

verdict.guard_found: main.go:27 exact map membership on u.Hostname() (images.example.org, docs.example.org). This validates only the initial URL. Nothing in the path re-checks the redirect hop, since http.Get at main.go:31 uses the default client, which follows redirects. Scheme is not restricted, but http.Get limits it to http/https.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches main.go: the query parameter is parsed at :26, the exact hostname check at :27 covers only the initial host, http.Get at :31 follows redirects to hosts that are never checked, and the body is returned at :37. The source is an unauthenticated query parameter on /safe, and the exact-host guard does not reach the redirect destination. The exploit still depends on an allowlisted host redirecting internally, which I could not verify from the code, so the finding's conditional severity (MEDIUM) stands.
